claims.text: Suppression of atomic diffusion due to severe lattice distortion and high configurational entropy is the primary factor governing structural and chemical stability in high-entropy nanoalloys at high temperature.
The relevant nanoalloys have near-equiatomic elemental mixing at the nanoscale.
The proposed comparison uses a near-equiatomic high-entropy sample and a modified, non-high-entropy sample with compositional segregation.
Temperature, atmosphere, and exposure time will be held constant between the high-entropy sample and the control.
High configurational entropy and associated lattice distortion produce sluggish atomic diffusion.
Near-equiatomic mixing induces significant lattice strain.
Near-equiatomic mixing creates a complex energy landscape that hinders atomic mobility.
Hindered atomic mobility suppresses grain-boundary migration during high-temperature exposure.
Hindered atomic mobility suppresses phase separation during high-temperature exposure.
Suppressed grain-boundary migration and phase separation enhance structural integrity and chemical homogeneity relative to a compositionally clustered nanoalloy.
The high-entropy nanoalloy will retain smaller grains than the control after high-temperature exposure.
The high-entropy nanoalloy will exhibit less compositional segregation than the control after high-temperature exposure.
Smaller retained grains and reduced segregation will yield superior structural and chemical stability under equal thermal stress.
The prediction is limited to high-temperature conditions in which near-equiatomic mixing is maintained.
The proposed mechanism may not apply outside the near-equiatomic composition range.
The proposed mechanism may not govern stability when aggressive oxidation or other phenomena dominate.
Oxidation kinetics may influence quantitative grain growth and segregation.
The relative contributions of sluggish diffusion and surface-energy effects are uncertain.
A lack of statistically significant reductions in both grain growth and compositional segregation relative to the control would falsify the hypothesis.
